points.description: States that the top of the stack is kept at the end (right side) of the array, so push and pop add/remove elements at the end of the array.
points.partial_credit: Half or more if it says push/pop work on the array but is vague or wrong about which end (e.g. only 'use an array with push and pop' or 'use a top index' without saying the end).

points.description: Names the two operations, push (add) and pop (remove), as acting on that end of the array.
points.partial_credit: Only one of push or pop mentioned correctly earns half.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying the top of the stack is at the end/right of the array and push and pop add and remove there, in any wording. Part marks for a vague or partly right idea, such as using an array with a top index but not saying the end. No marks for describing a different structure (e.g. a queue or linked list) or putting push/pop at the front.
